structured_output.hypothesis: If Darwin is right, nearly all oceanic islands and archipelagos of non-trivial size have native bats (the only native terrestrial mammals there), and many remote ones have endemic bat species or subspecies.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Reference set: oceanic (never continent-connected) islands or island groups with land area of at least 100 km², fixed in advance from a standard island list (for example, volcanic or coral islands in the Pacific, Atlantic and Indian Oceans). Using GBIF Chiroptera records (preserved specimen or human observation, with coordinates or an island/country field, excluding records flagged as introduced or as coordinate issues), at least 80% of the reference islands or groups have one or more native bat species. In addition, at least 40% of those more than 1000 km from the nearest continent have at least one bat taxon recorded only within that island group. Both thresholds must be met.
structured_output.fail_criterion: Fewer than 60% of the reference oceanic islands or groups have a native bat record, or fewer than 20% of the remote (more than 1000 km) ones have an endemic bat taxon. A result between the pass and fail thresholds counts as inconclusive, not as confirmation.
structured_output.interpretation: 'Ærial mammals' means Chiroptera. 'Oceanic islands' means islands never joined to a continent and far from one, as Darwin used the term. This is operationalised as volcanic or coral islands in a fixed pre-listed set, not continental-shelf islands, which would trivially hold bats. 'Almost every island' is read as a high proportion (at least 80%) of islands above a minimum size, because very small islets are not expected to hold populations. 'Own endemic bat species' is checked at species or subspecies level using current taxonomy, a modern reinterpretation of Darwin's 'modified in their new homes'. Records are filtered for introduced status, vagrants, and georeferencing errors. Fields used: taxonKey (Chiroptera), decimalLatitude, decimalLongitude, countryCode, islandGroup, island, establishmentMeans, basisOfRecord, scientificName, and the hasGeospatialIssue flag.

dataset.name: GBIF Occurrence Data (search and download service), filtered to order Chiroptera
dataset.why_it_fits: GBIF aggregates specimen and observation records of bats worldwide. Each record carries coordinates, country and island fields, and an establishmentMeans flag. The records can be downloaded through the occurrence search interface or API, then intersected with a fixed list of oceanic islands to test presence and endemism. A download request gets its own DOI, but the portal as a whole has none, so the DOI is null.
